description: Content defects surfaced by the 2026-07-30 citation-extraction pass over rules and signs. Each was found by a reviewer holding the question against Schedule 1 rather than against a prior summary, which is why they survived the earlier adversarial sweep.

set.prompt: A red rectangular sign with a single white arrow indicates:
set.explanation: The one-way roadway sign (R4) shows the single permitted direction of travel; no opposing traffic should be expected. It is not a heavy-vehicle restriction or a dead-end marker. Do not confuse its red background with the blue keep-left sign R103, which routes you around an obstacle.

ops.why: The prompt said 'a blue rectangular sign'. Schedule 1 gives R4 a RED retro-reflective background with a white arrow, and the project's own chart verdict for R4.1 records 'a red rectangular sign with a white horizontal arrow pointing left'. Blue is the keep-left sign R103. The keyed answer and the objective_code were right; the colour in the stem was wrong, which is the one detail a learner is being asked to recognise.

set.explanation: Permanent warning signs are red-bordered triangles standing on their base. A temporary roadworks warning is the same triangle on a yellow background (regulation 286A) — the background changes, the shape does not. A blue circle is a regulatory command sign.

ops.why: The explanation said 'the yellow diamond is reserved for temporary/roadworks warnings'. There is no yellow diamond warning sign in South Africa — that is the United States convention. Reg 286A(1)(b)(iii) makes a temporary sign a yellow-BACKGROUND version of the same triangle, with the red border retained. The keyed answer was always right; the contrast drawn to justify it was foreign signage.

set.explanation: The blue rectangular 'P' (R305-P) marks an area reserved for parking — it tells you parking is available, not that you must park there. The round 'P' in a red ring (R216) is the opposite: it prohibits parking.

ops.why: SECOND correction to this item today. The earlier rewrite fixed the keyed option but kept the explanation's claim that the rectangular P is an 'information sign'. Schedule 1 lists it as R305-P, a Regulatory 'Parking reservation sign' — 'Indicates to the driver of a vehicle that an area is reserved for parking'. It is regulatory, not information. Naming the code removes the class claim entirely rather than swapping one label for another.

Was W318, which the project's own chart verdict describes as 'Railway crossing ahead (UNCONTROLLED)' — the advance-warning triangle for a crossing with no gates or booms. This question is expressly about a boom coming down with flashing red lights, i.e. a controlled crossing, so W318 sent a learner who got it wrong to a lesson about the opposite case. Set to null rather than to a near-miss: W403/W404 are the St Andrew's cross markers, not the boom, and the operative signal (FRD-R1, used with stop sign R1) has no learning object. Null shows no recommendation, which is correct; a wrong code shows a confident wrong one. CONTENT GAP: there is no learning object for controlled level crossings.
